title: Choisir son point de repère
summary: Track plans seen from the past, since-clauses and dates relative to now or a narrative reference point.
objectives: Use imperfect `aller` + infinitive for a projected action in the past.
Distinguish speaker-relative time from narrative-relative dates and demonstratives.

sections.title: Was going to does not tell us the outcome
paragraphs: Imperfect `aller` + infinitive presents an intention or imminent event viewed from a past moment. The forms are `j'allais partir, tu allais partir, il/elle/on allait partir, nous allions partir, vous alliez partir, ils/elles allaient partir`: I/you/he etc. was/were going to leave. Only `aller` is conjugated; the next verb stays infinitive.

Context tells us whether the projected action happened. `J'allais sortir quand le téléphone a sonné` often describes an interruption, but `allait` does not inherently mean the plan failed. Negation can negate the projected action: `je n'allais pas accepter` means I was not going to accept.

examples.french: J'**allais fermer** quand un client est entré.
examples.english: I was about to close when a customer came in.
examples.note: A projected action is interrupted.

examples.french: Nous **allions visiter** le musée le lendemain ; la visite a été excellente.
examples.english: We were going to visit the museum the next day; the visit was excellent.
examples.note: The later context confirms the plan was fulfilled.

mistakes.why: Imperfect `aller` is followed by an infinitive, not a conjugated perfect form.

sections.title: Une intention ou un déplacement réel
paragraphs: `Aller` + infinitive can describe literal travel undertaken to do something as well as a projected action. `Je suis allé chercher un document` reports a completed trip to fetch a document; `j'allais chercher un document` can mean I was going to fetch it, or describe being on my way. A destination or a scene of movement helps identify the literal reading.

Do not convert every English 'was going to' into a past trip. If you need to make intention unmistakable, `j'avais l'intention de` is explicit. If you describe a completed trip, the `passé composé` of `aller` is appropriate. Neither a past intention nor travelling for a purpose alone guarantees that the purpose was achieved.

examples.french: J'**allais demander** une attestation, mais j'ai changé d'avis.
examples.english: I was going to request a certificate, but I changed my mind.
examples.note: The context presents an abandoned intention.

examples.french: Je **suis allée demander** une attestation à l'accueil, mais le guichet était fermé.
examples.english: I went to reception to request a certificate, but the counter was closed.
examples.note: A woman made the trip; she did not necessarily obtain the document.

examples.french: J'**allais chercher** mon fils à pied quand j'ai croisé la directrice.
examples.english: I was on my way to collect my son on foot when I met the headteacher.
examples.note: The imperfect can also describe actual movement in progress.

sections.title: `Depuis que` introduces a clause, not a duration noun
paragraphs: `Depuis que` means since/ever since and introduces a subject plus conjugated verb. The indicative is normal because the starting situation is presented as actual. `Depuis` without `que` introduces a date or duration: `depuis lundi`, `depuis deux mois`.

For a current continuing situation, French often uses present in the main clause: `je dors mieux depuis que j'ai changé de chambre`. A completed starting event can be `passé composé`; a continuing starting situation can be present. For a past viewpoint, use imperfect for the continuing background and often pluperfect for the earlier starting event. Completed counts or negated events may use compound past forms; `depuis que` does not impose one tense on every verb.

examples.french: Je dors mieux **depuis que j'ai changé** de chambre.
examples.english: I have been sleeping better since I changed rooms.
examples.note: Current continuing effect, completed starting event.

examples.french: **Depuis qu'elle travaille** ici, elle vient à vélo.
examples.english: Ever since she has been working here, she has been coming by bicycle.
examples.note: Both habits continue.

examples.french: Il dormait mieux **depuis qu'il avait réduit** le café.
examples.english: He had been sleeping better since he had cut down on coffee.
examples.note: Past continuing effect and earlier completed change.

examples.french: Nous avons reçu trois lettres **depuis que nous avons publié** l'annonce.
examples.english: We have received three letters since we published the notice.
examples.note: A count of completed events, not one continuing action.

mistakes.avoid: Je travaille ici depuis que deux mois.
mistakes.prefer: Je travaille ici depuis deux mois.
mistakes.why: A duration noun phrase takes `depuis` without `que`.

sections.title: Today versus the day you are talking about
paragraphs: `Hier` and `demain` normally refer to the day before and after the speaker's today. `La veille` (f.) and `le lendemain` (m.) refer to the day before and after an established event or narrative date. `Le jour précédent` and `le jour suivant` are explicit alternatives. In reported narration, shifting the reference point often changes `hier/demain` to `la veille/le lendemain`.
Keep `hier` or `demain` when you genuinely mean yesterday or tomorrow from the present speaker's viewpoint. Do not replace them mechanically in every sentence with a past verb.

examples.french: Nous sommes mardi : je partirai **demain**.
examples.english: It is Tuesday: I will leave tomorrow.
examples.note: Tomorrow is relative to now.

examples.french: Elle est arrivée le 4 mai et est repartie **le lendemain**.
examples.english: She arrived on 4 May and left the next day.
examples.note: The reference point makes this 5 May.

examples.french: La réunion était le vendredi ; j'avais confirmé **la veille**.
examples.english: The meeting was on Friday; I had confirmed the day before.
examples.note: The day before Friday, not necessarily yesterday.

sections.title: Nommer l'événement qui sert de repère
paragraphs: `La veille` and `le lendemain` can take `de` + an event noun, so the reference point need not be a date in a previous sentence. Use the normal contractions: `du` with `le`, `des` with `les`, but `de la` and `de l'`. `La veille au soir` singles out the previous evening. In conversation, `le jour d'avant` and `le jour d'après` can refer to the previous and following day when the reference is clear.

Distinguish `précédent`, an adjective meaning previous, from `précédant`, a present participle meaning preceding. The adjective agrees with a noun; the participle keeps `-ant` and can take a direct object. Ask whether the form simply labels a previous period or introduces what that period precedes. This is a difference in construction, not just an accent to memorize.

examples.french: La salle sera inspectée **la veille du salon**.
examples.english: The room will be inspected the day before the trade fair.
examples.note: `De` + `le salon` becomes `du salon`; the reference is an event.

examples.french: Le bilan sera publié **le lendemain de la clôture**.
examples.english: The results will be published the day after the closing.
examples.note: `La clôture` is feminine; `de la` stays separate.

examples.french: Le départ était prévu jeudi; nous avions préparé le repas **la veille au soir**.
examples.english: Departure was planned for Thursday; we had prepared the meal the evening before.
examples.note: Wednesday evening is identified without using the speaker-relative `hier soir`.

examples.french: Elle a appelé mardi. **Le jour d'après**, elle est passée nous voir.
examples.english: She called on Tuesday. The next day, she came to see us.
examples.note: A conversational alternative with a clear anchor.

examples.french: Les journées **précédentes** avaient été fraîches.
examples.english: The previous days had been cool.
examples.note: The adjective agrees with `journées`.

examples.french: Les journées **précédant l'ouverture** ont été consacrées aux essais.
examples.english: The days preceding the opening were devoted to testing.
examples.note: The invariable participle takes `l'ouverture` as its direct object.

mistakes.why: The event is introduced by `de`, which contracts with `le`.

sections.title: Quelques jours ou toute une époque
paragraphs: The noun determines the size of the period you point to. `Ces jours-là` usually identifies particular days; `à cette époque-là` and `en ce temps-là` can describe a broader era. They are not interchangeable merely because English uses 'in those days'. Establish what period your listener should picture.

For the ordinary demonstrative expression 'that year', use `cette année-là`, not `cet an-là`. `An` occurs in counting expressions such as `deux ans`, but the pointing expression here selects `année`. Neither `-là` nor `époque` makes the verb past automatically; a clearly identified future period is possible too.
points: `Une époque` (f.) is a period or era; `le temps` (m.) can refer to a broader time; `une année` (f.) is a year.

examples.french: Pendant mon enfance, **à cette époque-là**, le village n'avait pas de bibliothèque.
examples.english: During my childhood, in that period, the village had no library.
examples.note: A broad era rather than a few dates.

examples.french: Les ateliers auront lieu du 2 au 4 juillet. **Ces jours-là**, les portes resteront ouvertes.
examples.english: The workshops will run from 2 to 4 July. On those days, the doors will stay open.
examples.note: A short identified future period.

examples.french: La résidence ouvrira en 2028. **Cette année-là**, nous recruterons vingt personnes.
examples.english: The residence will open in 2028. That year, we will recruit twenty people.
examples.note: `Année` is feminine, and `-là` points to the specified future year.

examples.french: Les premières réunions se tenaient chez les habitants. **En ce temps-là**, nous n'avions pas de local.
examples.english: The first meetings took place in residents' homes. In those days, we had no premises.
examples.note: A broader earlier period; not a count of individual days.

sections.title: This period and that period
paragraphs: A demonstrative determiner points to an identifiable noun: `ce` with masculine singular, `cet` before a masculine vowel or mute `h`, `cette` with feminine singular, `ces` with either plural. Add `-ci` or `-là` to the end of the time noun with a hyphen to distinguish the current/near period from another identified period.

Useful nouns: `un jour` (m.), `une semaine` (f.), `un été` (m.), `une année` (f.). `Ce jour-là` means on that day; `ces jours-ci` often means these days/around now, not a mathematically fixed duration. `-Là` can refer backward in a narrative or to another specified period; it does not inherently mean past.

examples.french: **Cette semaine-ci**, nous travaillons à distance.
examples.english: This week, we are working remotely.
examples.note: Explicitly identifies the current week.

examples.french: Nous nous sommes rencontrés en 2018. **Cet été-là**, il faisait très chaud.
examples.english: We met in 2018. That summer, it was very hot.
examples.note: `Cet` before `été`; `-là` identifies the narrated summer.

examples.french: Je suis très occupé **ces jours-ci**.
examples.english: I am very busy these days.
examples.note: A current period, not a named date.

examples.french: La fête aura lieu en juillet. **Ce jour-là**, le parc sera fermé aux voitures.
examples.english: The festival will take place in July. On that day, the park will be closed to cars.
examples.note: `-Là` can identify a future day.

practice.prompt: What is established by Je suis allé acheter des piles, mais le magasin était fermé?
choices: The trip happened; the purchase is not established.
The speaker only thought about leaving home.
answers: The trip happened; the purchase is not established.
practice.explanation: Passé composé aller reports the trip; acheter gives its purpose, not guaranteed success.

practice.prompt: Express a past intention, not a completed trip, using imperfect aller + proposer: Nous ___ un échange, puis nous avons abandonné cette idée.
practice.explanation: The prompt selects the projected-action reading and the imperfect.

practice.prompt: A woman reports her completed trip, not just a plan. Supply aller in the passé composé: Je ___ déposer le dossier à la mairie.
practice.explanation: A completed trip uses suis allée; the infinitive describes its purpose.

practice.prompt: Complete with the needed contracted de + article: La veille ___ départ, nous avons pesé les bagages.
practice.explanation: Le départ is masculine; de + le contracts to du.

practice.prompt: Use the adjective précédent, agreeing with semaines: Les deux semaines ___ avaient été calmes.
practice.explanation: An adjective agrees with its feminine plural noun.

practice.prompt: Translate only 'the day after the opening' using lendemain. L'ouverture is feminine.
practice.explanation: The event follows de; l' does not contract with de.

practice.prompt: Use the present participle of précéder, not the adjective: Les jours ___ la fermeture ont été très chargés.
practice.explanation: Précédant takes la fermeture as its object and stays invariable.

practice.prompt: Supply 'the evening before' using la veille + au soir: L'examen était mardi matin; elle avait relu ses notes ___.
practice.explanation: The phrase identifies Monday evening relative to the exam.

practice.prompt: Use lendemain + de to say 'the day after the elections'. Supply the whole noun phrase.
practice.explanation: De + plural les contracts to des.

practice.prompt: Use année and -là to refer back to 2021: Nous avons ouvert en 2021. ___, les commandes arrivaient par courrier. Supply 'that year'.
practice.explanation: The ordinary demonstrative time phrase uses feminine année, not an.

practice.prompt: Which expression naturally introduces a broad period of childhood rather than a few specific days?
practice.explanation: Une époque is a broader period; ces jours-là identifies particular days.

practice.prompt: Refer specifically to three identified days using jours and -là: Les 6, 7 et 8 août sont réservés. ___, le centre accueillera les équipes. Supply 'on those days'.
practice.explanation: Ces jours-là points to the three stated days; no additional preposition is needed.

practice.prompt: Supply aller + partir for 'we were going to leave', without subject: Nous ___ quand elle est arrivée.
practice.explanation: Imperfect aller + infinitive.

practice.prompt: Supply only the connector meaning 'since': Je lis plus ___ j'ai arrêté la télévision. A clause follows.
practice.explanation: A finite clause needs depuis que.

practice.prompt: The story is about last year. Replace 'the next day' with the conventional two-word expression beginning le: Elle est arrivée le 8 juin et est partie ___.
practice.explanation: The reference is 8 June, not today; the two-word constraint identifies le lendemain rather than le jour suivant.

practice.prompt: Supply the complete phrase 'that summer' using été and -là.
practice.explanation: Été is masculine and begins with a vowel.

practice.prompt: Supply aller + répondre for 'you were going to reply', with vous already given: Vous ___ quand la connexion a coupé.
practice.explanation: Alliez plus an infinitive.

practice.prompt: Supply travailler in the present for a continuing situation: Je ___ ici depuis que j'ai quitté Lyon.
practice.explanation: French present expresses a situation continuing now.

practice.prompt: Supply déménager in the pluperfect: Elle marchait plus depuis qu'elle ___ près du parc.
practice.explanation: Earlier move, past continuing consequence.

practice.prompt: Use the noun expression beginning la for 'the day before': Le concert était le 12 ; nous avions répété ___.
practice.explanation: The day before the stated concert.

practice.prompt: Build 'this week' with semaine and explicit -ci.
practice.explanation: Semaine is feminine; -ci follows the noun.

practice.prompt: Build the usual phrase 'these days' with jours and -ci.
practice.explanation: Plural ces and hyphenated -ci.

practice.prompt: Does Elle allait téléphoner prove that she never called?
choices: No; context supplies the eventual outcome.
Yes; allait always means the plan failed.
answers: No; context supplies the eventual outcome.
practice.explanation: The form projects from the past without fixing the outcome.

practice.prompt: Can ce jour-là refer to a future festival day?
choices: Yes, if that future day is identified.
answers: Yes, if that future day is identified.
practice.explanation: Reference and tense are distinct.

practice.prompt: Today is Thursday. Supply one word for the speaker's yesterday: J'ai envoyé le dossier ___, mercredi.
practice.explanation: Hier refers to the day before the speaker's today.

practice.prompt: Replace la veille with the equivalent expression using jour + précédent. Supply the whole phrase.
practice.explanation: The day preceding an established reference date, not necessarily yesterday.

practice.prompt: Supply aller + commencer for 'they were about to begin': Ils ___ quand l'alarme a sonné.
practice.explanation: Imperfect aller with an infinitive.

practice.prompt: Today is Monday. Supply one word meaning tomorrow: Je viendrai ___, mardi.
practice.explanation: The reference is the speaker's today.

practice.prompt: Replace le lendemain with the equivalent expression using jour + suivant. Supply the whole expression.
practice.explanation: Both refer to the day following an established date.

practice.prompt: Supply only depuis or depuis que: Il habite ici ___ trois ans.
practice.explanation: A duration is not a clause.

production_task.prompt: Tell a short story about a planned visit last year. Identify the day, a projected action, an earlier change introduced with `depuis que`, and what happened the following day.
production_task.model_answer: Nous sommes arrivés le 10 avril. Ce jour-là, nous allions visiter le port, mais il pleuvait. Depuis que ma sœur avait vendu sa voiture, nous voyagions en train. Le lendemain, le ciel était clair et nous avons fait une longue promenade.
production_task.translation: We arrived on 10 April. That day, we were going to visit the harbour, but it was raining. Since my sister had sold her car, we had been travelling by train. The next day, the sky was clear and we went for a long walk.
rubric: The narrative reference point is explicit.
`Depuis que` links actual situations on a coherent timeline.
`Le lendemain` and `ce jour-là` refer back clearly.
